**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right running against Bluefly. Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "monitor" and "premises" turned up nothing usable, and the sections that could plausibly host such a right (§ 4 charges/payment, § 11.5 Capacity Planning, § 12.1 License, §§ 13–14 general terms) contain none.

The planner's likely hook, § 11.3 Suspected Violations, is a breach-remedy provision only: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the § 11.2(b) content warranties and then restrict access to the Services, require removal of Content, terminate, or pursue other remedies — with an undertaking to attempt notice before restricting access or removing Content. It gives IBM no access to our systems, personnel, books or records, and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden on us.

That leaves us better off than the AUDIT preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so inserting an audit framework would only manufacture a right IBM does not have. I noted in the rationale, as a non-deviation observation, that § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts only — acceptable given it carries no entry into our environment.
